meters.label: Keys proven equal by hashes alone

frames.narration: Two replicas hold the same 1,000,000 keys. While B is down, 5 writes reach A only and the hints for B are lost.
B returns. Reads do not touch those 5 keys, so nothing fixes them. Comparing every key would move about 100 MB, so each replica keeps a Merkle tree over 1,024 key ranges (about 977 keys each).
The repair job asks both replicas for their root hash: 32 bytes each. The roots differ, so the replicas differ somewhere.
It asks for the two children of the root. One matches and is pruned, so half the keys are never examined. The other differs, so it is opened.
At each of the 10 levels only the differing nodes are opened, 2 hashes each. The 5 bad keys sit in 5 different ranges, so the descent needs 79 hash comparisons in total, about 2.5 KB.
The job now has the 5 differing leaf ranges. Everything else, about 995,000 keys, was proven equal by hashes alone.
A streams the 5 ranges, about 4,900 keys or 488 KB, and B reconciles them with its normal rule (last write wins by timestamp). The whole store was never scanned over the network.

After the repair B rebuilds those 5 leaves and their paths to the root. The roots now match, so the next check costs one 32 byte comparison. The expensive part was reading data to build the trees, not the network.
